extra.message: Insecure deserialization via pickle in ops console — Remote code execution for anyone possessing or guessing the static internal token [verified: pickle.loads runs on raw request body/GET-controlled bytes with no validation; static token gate is a weak, brute-forceable control, not a compensating control for RCE.]

Server-side template injection in ops console — Remote code execution via Jinja2 sandbox escape / arbitrary template expression evaluation [verified: Jinja2 Template is built by string concatenation of request-controlled fragment then rendered, enabling SSTI/RCE via template expressions.]

OS command injection in ops console ping utility — Arbitrary command execution on the server via the host parameter [verified: os.system concatenates unsanitized GET host param directly into a shell command with no escaping or allow-list.]

Authorization header logged in plaintext — Bearer tokens/credentials sent to this endpoint are persisted into application logs, which are often broader-access than the API itself, enabling credential theft via log access [verified: logger.warning logs the raw Authorization header and full body at WARNING level with no redaction.]

Sensitive data (Authorization header) written to logs — Anyone with log access can obtain bearer tokens/credentials sent in the Authorization header [verified: Duplicate of idx 9: logger.warning call confirmed logging body and Authorization header unredacted.]

Path traversal and plaintext PII storage via ref parameter — Arbitrary file write outside intended directory and plaintext storage of sensitive SSN/card data readable by anyone with filesystem access [verified: Duplicate of idx 3: ref-based path traversal plus plaintext SSN/card storage confirmed in code at lines 92-95.]

Forgeable client-supplied cookie/header grants elevated data access — Any caller who passes the static ops token gate can trivially set Cookie: ops_badge=lead or X-Ops-Badge: lead to obtain the 'elevated' payroll/casework response, bypassing any intended internal privilege tiering [verified: Elevated payroll data is gated solely by a client-supplied cookie/header equal to 'lead', with no server-side identity/role verification.]

Path traversal / arbitrary file write via name parameter — Arbitrary file write anywhere the app process can write, potentially overwriting application code or planting a web shell [verified: Duplicate of idx 2: name joined directly onto BASE_EXPORT_DIR with no sanitization, raw POST body written to resulting path.]

Insecure DEBUG and SECRET_KEY defaults — Verbose Django debug pages expose source, environment and settings if DEBUG stays True in production; a known/default SECRET_KEY enables forging signed sessions/cookies [verified: DEBUG defaults to True via os.environ.get('DEBUG','True') and SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded insecure default, matching the committed .env.example, so an operator who omits these env vars in production gets debug pages and a predictable key.]

IDOR on document_download bypasses org/assignment scoping — Support agents can read confidential documents (contracts, security docs) belonging to organizations they have no relationship with [verified: document_download for support_agent only excludes VISIBILITY_BILLING but never checks org relationship (contrast document_list:483-487), so any support agent can fetch any org's internal/contract docs by UUID.]

Mass assignment overwrites arbitrary existing users via CSV contact import — An account_manager importing a crafted CSV can change another user's email (enabling password-reset takeover), re-parent them to a different organization, and demote/overwrite their profile fields [verified: import_contacts update_or_create keys solely on CSV-supplied username with no ownership check, silently overwriting an existing user's email/org/role fields, enabling account takeover via password reset on the changed email.]

Open redirect in ops console — Attacker crafts a link through a trusted internal domain to redirect victims to phishing/malicious sites [verified: redirect(next_url) uses the raw 'lane' GET param with no allow-list or same-origin validation, enabling open redirect.]

Missing authentication gate on ops endpoint — Unauthenticated attacker can reach an internal ops endpoint and queue actions (handle/channel), bypassing the internal-token control applied to every sibling endpoint [verified: acct_identity_ping_343 (line 106) has no _wrk_gate call unlike every sibling handler, confirmed missing from the source, making it reachable without the internal token.]

Hardcoded low-entropy verifier codes used as an auth check — An attacker holding the internal ops token can brute-force the 4-digit verifier (max 10,000 attempts, no throttling) to pass this identity check for 'north'/'south' handles [verified: 4-digit verifier codes are hardcoded and checked with non-constant-time comparison with no rate limiting, brute-forceable within 10,000 requests.]

CORS misconfiguration allows credentialed cross-origin reads — Any external origin can make credentialed cross-origin requests and read responses, exfiltrating session-authenticated data [verified: Origin header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin alongside Allow-Credentials: true, permitting credentialed cross-origin reads from any origin.]

TLS certificate verification disabled for outbound request — Man-in-the-middle attacker on the network path can intercept/tamper with the outbound partner request/response [verified: Duplicate of idx 7: ssl._create_unverified_context() confirmed passed to urlopen for the outbound partner request.]

Missing ownership check allows deal creation for any organization — An account manager can create Deal records tied to another account manager's organization, corrupting financial/deal data across tenants [verified: deal_create checks only role, not that DealForm's organization belongs to the account manager, unlike deal_edit/deal_detail which check organization.account_manager != request.user.]

Missing ownership check allows escalation creation for any organization — Any authenticated account_manager or support_agent can create escalations (and assign arbitrary agents) inside organizations they do not manage, polluting/manipulating another tenant's escalation queue [verified: escalation_create only blocks customer_contact and calls form.save() with an EscalationForm whose organization field is unrestricted, unlike escalation_edit/status_change which check organization.account_manager != request.user.]

API key revocation triggerable via CSRF/GET — Attacker can revoke a victim's API key via a crafted link/image, causing denial of service to legitimate integrations [verified: apikey_revoke mutates state on any HTTP method with no CSRF-relevant method check, so a GET-based cross-site request revokes a victim's key.]

API key rotation triggerable via CSRF/GET — Attacker forces key rotation cross-site, breaking legitimate API consumers and enabling confusion attacks [verified: apikey_rotate mutates and saves a new key on any method, so a cross-site GET can force rotation and break the victim's integration.]

Hardcoded default password for imported contacts — Account takeover of freshly-imported customer contacts via a known default password [verified: import_contacts sets a fixed literal password 'changeme123' for every newly created contact with no forced reset, enabling takeover before the real user logs in.]

Weak hash algorithm (MD5) used for verifier digest — Digests can be reversed via rainbow tables or brute force, defeating any secrecy/integrity guarantee intended by the hash [verified: hashlib.md5 used on a user-supplied phrase as a 'digest' with no salt or modern KDF, confirmed at line 103.]

Non-constant-time comparison of verifier secret — An attacker able to measure response timing could incrementally brute-force the verifier value character by character [verified: verifier != known[handle] uses Python's standard string inequality, which short-circuits on first mismatch and is not constant-time.]

Predictable PRNG used for nonce/code generation — If this nonce is used anywhere as a security token, its future/past values can be predicted, defeating its purpose as an unguessable identifier [verified: random.choice (Mersenne Twister) is used to generate a security-sounding nonce/code, which is predictable, not cryptographically secure.]

Webhook test delivery triggerable via CSRF/GET — Attacker can trigger spurious outbound webhook calls and audit log noise on behalf of a victim user [verified: webhook_test creates a WebhookDelivery without checking request.method, allowing GET-based CSRF to trigger deliveries under the victim's session.]

CSV formula injection in renewals export — Formula execution / data exfiltration or code execution in the spreadsheet application of whoever opens the exported CSV (e.g. platform admin) [verified: org.name and billing_contact fields are user-controlled via OrganizationForm and written raw into CSV via csv.writer with no leading-character sanitization.]

CSV formula injection in escalations export — Formula execution / data exfiltration in spreadsheet app of the user opening the export [verified: esc.title and org.name are user-controlled and written raw into CSV rows with no formula-injection sanitization.]

CSV formula injection in health report export — Formula execution / data exfiltration in spreadsheet app of the platform admin opening the export [verified: org.internal_notes is a free-text user-controlled field written raw into CSV with no sanitization, executed when opened by a platform admin.]
